# Impact of Cobalt Content on EV Battery Energy Density

## High Cobalt Content → Higher Energy Density

**Positive effects of increased cobalt:**

| Factor | Impact |
|--------|--------|
| **Structural stability** | Cobalt stabilizes the layered crystal structure of cathodes |
| **Voltage** | Enables higher operating voltage (~4.2V vs ~3.7V) |
| **Capacity** | Allows more lithium ions to be extracted/inserted |
| **Cycle efficiency** | Reduces structural degradation during charging |

## The Trade-off Spectrum

```
High Cobalt (LCO)          →          Low/No Cobalt (LFP)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Higher energy density                Lower energy density
~250-300 Wh/kg                       ~150-180 Wh/kg
Higher cost                          Lower cost
Less thermal stability               Better safety
```

## Common Chemistries by Cobalt Content

- **LCO** (100% cobalt in cathode): ~250-300 Wh/kg
- **NMC 111**: Balanced Co/Ni/Mn
- **NMC 532/622**: Reduced cobalt
- **NMC 811**: ~8% cobalt, ~270-300 Wh/kg
- **LFP** (zero cobalt): ~150-180 Wh/kg

## Industry Trend

Manufacturers are reducing cobalt due to **cost** and **ethical sourcing concerns**, compensating with higher nickel content and advanced engineering to maintain energy density.
